test_purpose: Establish a trustworthy, reproducible, non-contaminated baseline of the 328 authoritative Easy Query set against the CURRENT LIVE PRODUCTION Curify search, before any search-relevance optimization work (Rewrite Guard, protected-phrase dictionary, d/g toggles, new CJK tokenizer, etc.) is merged, so future optimized-version runs have a valid 'before' to compare against.
baseline_definition: The code currently deployed and serving https://www.curify-ai.com, independently confirmed (not assumed) via GitHub Deployments API + origin/main HEAD match + vercel.json deployment rules to be commit 72b55b667bb5173cab87fcec377198064dc3ac28. Explicitly NOT the local uncommitted/unpushed baobao/search-relevance-phrase-alias-2026-07-09 branch.
collection_target: live production website (GET page navigation, real Chromium browser)
retry_policy: max 2 attempts, network/timeout errors only; zero/low-result outcomes never retried
checkpoint_policy: one JSON record written immediately per completed query, plus a rollup checkpoint file every 10 completed queries
interruption_detail: Background process was killed by an environment/session restart at query_index 152/328 (browser context closed mid-navigation). 151 valid completed records existed at that point. Run was restarted and correctly resumed from query 152 with zero re-execution of 1-151 and zero duplicate output files. Full detail in logs/resume_history.md.
post_run_targeted_repair: After full completion, a DOM-extraction bug was found affecting the broadened_query/raw_rewrite_visible text (not result counts) for 17/139 broadened records (over-capture of a large ancestor element instead of the specific banner div). The extraction logic was fixed and exactly those 17 raw/*.json files were deleted and regenerated via a live re-query (resume logic skipped the other 311 unaffected records). Full detail in logs/resume_history.md. Final counts below reflect the post-repair state.
LLM_used_by_production_search_detail: lib/searchRewrite.ts calls OpenAI gpt-4o-mini server-side for thin-result queries; pre-existing production behavior since 2026-05-18, not part of the excluded optimization branch.
raw_response_format: one structured JSON record per query in raw/<query_index>_<easy_id>.json
screenshot_policy: full-page screenshot saved for every query (not only failures)
warnings: result_count_reported (a UI-visible numeric total) is not exposed anywhere on the production search page; result_count_observed (actual rendered card count) is used as the operative metric throughout instead — recorded as null rather than guessed.

filter_state and pagination_state are null for all records — production's search results page has neither filters nor pagination (confirmed by source audit), so there is nothing to record, not a collection gap.
spelling_correction_visible is null for all records — could not be distinguished as a signal separate from the general rewrite/broaden banner without risking a false positive.

17 records (E008, E010, E013, E014, E018, E020, E022, E035, E058, E081, E144, E145, E290, E297, E301, E304, E317) were re-collected once, live, after a targeted extraction-bug fix (see post_run_targeted_repair above); their final_status/result_count reflects the second live query, which for a small subset differs slightly from the first-pass value due to production's non-zero-temperature LLM rewriter, not a data-quality defect.
unresolved_uncertainties: OPENAI_API_KEY / LLM rewrite success rate on Vercel's production environment was not directly inspected (no access to Vercel env vars) — LLM-rewrite behavior is inferred from observable banner text and source code, not from a Vercel-side log.

The 2026-07-14 optimized-code comparison run used the LOCAL, unpushed optimization branch, not a deployed version — so summaries/baseline_vs_optimized_join_ready.csv is a code-path comparison (production vs. local candidate), not a temporal same-deployment before/after; this is flagged in that file's comparison_warning column for every row.
